meta.audience: The survivors, and then the reader
meta.location: The whole land, in the dark and then the morning
meta.date: AD 34, the end of the three days
meta.unit: The destruction and the visit (3 Nephi 8–11)
principles: A gathering offered three times in three tenses
Survival explained by what the survivors did not do

world_behind.title: The silence lasts hours
world_behind.text: Verses 1 and 2 say astonishment stopped the lamenting for many hours. 3 Nephi 8:23 has that mourning running continually through three days of darkness, so this is the first quiet the land has had since the storm.

world_behind.title: The second voice uses one image three times
world_behind.text: Verses 4, 5, and 6 give the hen and chickens in past, past-conditional, and future. Matthew 23:37 and Luke 13:34 both carry the figure once, addressed to Jerusalem and in one tense; this passage uses it three times and moves the tense each time.

world_behind.title: Jerusalem is addressed alongside them
world_behind.text: Verse 5 speaks to the house of Israel at Jerusalem in the same sentence as the fallen here.

world_behind.title: The weeping resumes
world_behind.text: Verse 8 has them howling again after the voice finishes. 3 Nephi 8:23 to 25 records the same weeping before the voice came, so the chapter has grief on both sides of the message rather than resolved by it.

world_behind.title: The earth closes
world_behind.text: Verses 9 and 10 have the darkness dispersing, the rending stopping, and the ground cleaving together again. 3 Nephi 8:17 and 18 had the face of the whole earth deformed and the rocks broken into seams and cracks, and the reversal is reported clause for clause against that description.

world_behind.title: The survivors are defined negatively
world_behind.text: Verse 12 has them receiving the prophets, refusing to stone them, and keeping clear of the saints' blood. Helaman 13:24 had charged the previous generation with casting out the prophets and stoning them, so the survival criterion is the exact reverse of the standing indictment.

world_behind.title: Mormon addresses the reader directly
world_behind.text: Verse 14 tells whoever reads to search the scriptures and check these events against the prophecies.

words.text: Treated at Alma 55:17, of a night attack. Verse 1 uses it of a whole land that stopped making noise, and verse 2 gives astonishment as the cause.
Mourning aloud. The record uses the word twice, here and at Alma 18:43, and the King James Bible never. Verse 2 records it stopping rather than starting.
A mother bird. All four of the record's uses are in this chapter, and the King James Bible has three, including Matthew 23:37, which the image here follows closely.
Loud grieving. It appears twice, here and at Alma 40:13, in the record, and the King James Bible sixteen times. Verse 10 has it ceasing and turning to praise.
Pressed to death. The word occurs once in the record and seven times in the King James Bible. Verse 13 lists it among six deaths the spared did not die.
Going up. The word turns up four times here, and the King James Bible never. Verse 18 dates the visit to soon after it.

phrases.term: There was silence in the land for the space of many hours
phrases.text: The response to the voice, stated twice in two verses. Revelation 8:1 measures a silence in heaven the same way.

phrases.term: They did cease lamenting and howling for the loss of their kindred
phrases.text: What the silence interrupted. Grief already in progress stopped, which is how the record measures the astonishment.

phrases.term: How oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings
phrases.text: The first of three. This one is past tense, and adds that he nourished them.

phrases.term: How oft would I have gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens, and ye would not
phrases.text: The second, in the words Matthew 23:37 gives over Jerusalem. Verse 5 addresses both cities in one sentence.

phrases.term: If ye will repent and return unto me with full purpose of heart
phrases.text: The third, in the future, and the only one with a condition. 2 Nephi 31:13 uses the same phrase of coming to baptism.

phrases.term: They began to weep and howl again because of the loss of their kindred and friends
phrases.text: The silence ends and the grief comes back. The record does not report a conversion at this point.

phrases.term: The earth did cleave together again, that it stood
phrases.text: The ground closing after three days. The same verse has the mourning turn into praise and thanksgiving.

phrases.term: Thus far were the scriptures fulfilled
phrases.text: Mormon marking a checkpoint. What follows in verses 14 through 17 is an argument that the reader can verify.

phrases.term: It was they who received the prophets and stoned them not
phrases.text: The survivors described by two things they refrained from doing. 3 Nephi 9:11 had made casting out the prophets the reason a city burned.

phrases.term: Whoso readeth, let him understand; he that hath the scriptures, let him search them
phrases.text: Mormon handing the argument to the reader. Matthew 24:15 uses the first clause word for word.

phrases.term: Are not we a remnant of the seed of Joseph?
phrases.text: A question rather than a claim. Verse 17 grounds it in the plates of brass that Lehi carried out of Jerusalem.

verses.label: v. 1–2
verses.title: Hours of quiet, and what stopped the noise
verses.text: The record gives the interval a duration: "there was silence in the land for the space of many hours." Verse 2 explains what stopped the noise, and the explanation is not comfort: "so great was the astonishment of the people that they did cease lamenting and howling for the loss of their kindred which had been slain." The mourning of 3 Nephi 8:23–25 ends because something more startling has happened, not because the grief has passed, and verse 8 reports it resuming.

verses.label: v. 4–6
verses.title: One image, three times, in three tenses
verses.text: The record works a single simile through past, conditional and future in consecutive verses: "how oft have I gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and have nourished you"; "how oft would I have gathered you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings"; "how oft will I gather you as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, if ye will repent." The figure stands once in the Bible, at Matt. 23:37, in the conditional form only. Here the record conjugates it, and the third instance carries the condition the other two lack.

verses.label: v. 9–10
verses.title: The undoing reported item by item
verses.text: The record reverses the destruction of 3 Nephi 8 by listing each element as it stops: "the darkness dispersed from off the face of the land, and the earth did cease to tremble, and the rocks did cease to rend, and the dreadful groanings did cease, and all the tumultuous noises did pass away." Verse 10 completes it with the physical repair, "the earth did cleave together again, that it stood." Five things end and one thing is restored, and the order runs from the sky down to the ground.

verses.label: v. 11–13
verses.title: The survivors identified by one test, stated twice
verses.text: The record does not describe the spared population by number or by place. It gives a criterion: "it was the more righteous part of the people who were saved, and it was they who received the prophets and stoned them not." Verse 13 then lists what they escaped in the same terms the previous chapter used for the destruction, "they were not sunk and buried up in the earth... not drowned in the depths of the sea... not burned by fire." Treatment of prophets is the only variable named on either side.

verses.label: v. 14
verses.title: An instruction to go and check
verses.text: One verse addresses the reader directly and tells him to verify the account against another book: "whoso readeth, let him understand; he that hath the scriptures, let him search them, and see and behold if all these deaths and destructions by fire, and by smoke, and by tempests, and by whirlwinds... be not unto the fulfilling of the prophecies of many of the holy prophets." The record makes its own claim testable and names the test.

verses.label: v. 15–17
verses.title: Three witnesses named, and two of them have no book
verses.text: The record supplies the prophets it means: "the prophet Zenos did testify of these things, and also Zenock spake concerning these things," and then "our father Jacob also testified concerning a remnant of the seed of Joseph." Zenos and Zenock appear in the Bible nowhere at all, and the third is the volume's own patriarch. Verse 15 also states what happened to the witnesses, "many have testified of these things at the coming of Christ, and were slain because they testified of these things."

verses.label: v. 18–19
verses.title: A chapter closed by an announcement of the next one
verses.text: The last two verses report a visit and then defer it: the people "did see and hear him, inasmuch as they were spared," and then "an account of his ministry shall be given hereafter." The record names what it is postponing and why it is stopping: "Therefore for this time I make an end of my sayings." A compiler is dividing his material and telling the reader where the seam is.

chapter.title: The response to the voice is silence
chapter.text: Not repentance, not argument. Verses 1 and 2 say it twice and give astonishment as the cause.

chapter.title: The same image is used in three tenses
chapter.text: Have gathered, would have gathered, will gather. Only the third carries a condition, and it is the one addressed to the living.

chapter.title: Two hemispheres are addressed in a single line
chapter.text: Verse 5 speaks to those at Jerusalem and those fallen here together, in the words Matthew records over Jerusalem (Matt. 23:37).

chapter.title: Grief resumes after the voice
chapter.text: Verse 8 has them weeping again. The record does not tidy the sequence into a conversion.

chapter.title: The turn happens with the daylight
chapter.text: Verse 10 has mourning becoming praise in the same sentence as the earth closing.

chapter.title: The spared are identified by omissions
chapter.text: Verse 12 names what they did not do to the prophets, and verse 13 names six deaths they did not die.

chapter.title: Mormon hands the reader the test
chapter.text: Verse 14 says search the scriptures and check. The argument is offered as verifiable rather than asserted.

chapter.title: Two prophets outside the Bible are the evidence
chapter.text: Verse 16 names two prophets who appear in no surviving Bible and states what makes them relevant, "they testified particularly concerning us, who are the remnant of their seed." Verse 17 adds a third, "our father Jacob also testified concerning a remnant of the seed of Joseph," and names the source, "written upon the plates of brass." 1 Nephi 19:10 had cited the same two, Zenos and Zenock, for the same kind of claim eight hundred years earlier in the record. The evidence offered for a people's identity is a text nobody outside these books has.

applications.title: Let silence be a real response
applications.text: A whole land stopped making noise for hours. Some things are answered first by not speaking.

applications.title: Notice which offer has the condition
applications.text: The past gatherings are stated; the future one depends on returning with full purpose of heart. Mercy already given and mercy still open are different sentences.

applications.title: Expect grief to come back after the meaning arrives
applications.text: They heard the voice and then wept again. Understanding a loss does not finish it.

applications.title: Let the mourning end when it ends
applications.text: The earth cleaved together again, and the weeping of the people who were spared ceased and turned into praise. Grief does not have to be sustained to prove it was real, and the record marks the turn without apologizing for it.

applications.title: The survivors are described by a behavior
applications.text: The spared are named as those who received the prophets and stoned them not. That is a criterion anybody can audit in themselves this week, which is presumably why it is the one given.

applications.title: Check the claim yourself
applications.text: Mormon tells the reader to search the scriptures and see. An argument offered for testing is worth more than one offered for acceptance.

applications.title: Some testimony costs the witness
applications.text: Many testified of these things at the coming of Christ, and the same verse says they were slain for testifying. The record keeps the price attached to the testimony instead of reporting only its content.

applications.title: Ask carefully whether the old text is about you
applications.text: Mormon points to Jacob's word about a remnant of the seed of Joseph and asks whether they are not that remnant. Reading yourself into an ancient promise is a move worth making with the text open in front of you, which is how he makes it.

questions.text: When did something stop me talking?
What has been offered to me repeatedly that I would not take?
What would returning with full purpose of heart mean this week?
What grief have I expected to be finished and is not?
What am I spared from, and what did I not do to deserve it?
What have I accepted without searching it out?
What am I a remnant of?
